informal_statement:
There exists a surjective group homomorphism from the Standard Model gauge group, SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1), to the Georgi-Glashow gauge group, SU(5), defined by mapping an element (h, g, α) ∈ SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) to the block diagonal matrix 
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\alpha^3 g & 0 \\
0 & \alpha^{-2} h
\end{pmatrix}
\]
This homomorphism plays a crucial role in embedding the gauge symmetry of the Standard Model into the larger symmetry of the Georgi-Glashow model.
informal_proof:
Let \( G = SU(3) \times SU(2) \times U(1) \) and \( H = SU(5) \). Define a map \( \phi: G \rightarrow H \) by
\[
\phi(h, g, \alpha) = \begin{pmatrix}
\alpha^3 g & 0 \\
0 & \alpha^{-2} h
\end{pmatrix}
\]
where \( h \in SU(3) \), \( g \in SU(2) \), and \( \alpha \in U(1) \).

**Step 1: Well-definedness**

Since \( \alpha^3 \) and \( \alpha^{-2} \) are scalar matrices in \( SU(5) \), multiplying \( g \in SU(2) \) by \( \alpha^3 \) and \( h \in SU(3) \) by \( \alpha^{-2} \) results in unitary matrices, ensuring \( \phi(h, g, \alpha) \in H \).

**Step 2: Homomorphism**

Take \( (h_1, g_1, \alpha_1), (h_2, g_2, \alpha_2) \in G \). Compute:
\[
\phi((h_1, g_1, \alpha_1) \cdot (h_2, g_2, \alpha_2)) = \phi(h_1 h_2, g_1 g_2, \alpha_1 \alpha_2)
\]
\[
= \begin{pmatrix}
(\alpha_1 \alpha_2)^3 g_1 g_2 & 0 \\
0 & (\alpha_1 \alpha_2)^{-2} h_1 h_2
\end{pmatrix}
\]
\[
= \begin{pmatrix}
\alpha_1^3 \alpha_2^3 g_1 g_2 & 0 \\
0 & \alpha_1^{-2} \alpha_2^{-2} h_1 h_2
\end{pmatrix}
\]
\[
= \begin{pmatrix}
\alpha_1^3 g_1 & 0 \\
0 & \alpha_1^{-2} h_1
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
\alpha_2^3 g_2 & 0 \\
0 & \alpha_2^{-2} h_2
\end{pmatrix}
\]
\[
= \phi(h_1, g_1, \alpha_1) \cdot \phi(h_2, g_2, \alpha_2)
\]
Thus, \( \phi \) preserves the group operation.

**Step 3: Surjectivity**

For any \( A = \begin{pmatrix} a & 0 \\ 0 & b \end{pmatrix} \in H \), where \( a \in SU(2) \) and \( b \in SU(3) \), there exists \( \alpha \in U(1) \) such that \( \alpha^3 a \in SU(2) \) and \( \alpha^{-2} b \in SU(3) \). Choosing \( h = \alpha^{-3} (\alpha^3 a) \), \( g = \alpha^{-3} (\alpha^3 a) \), and \( \alpha \) appropriately, we recover \( A \), hence \( \phi \) is surjective.

**Step 4: Kernel**

The kernel of \( \phi \) consists of all \( (h, g, \alpha) \) with \( \alpha^3 g = I_2 \) and \( \alpha^{-2} h = I_3 \). Since \( g = \alpha^{-3} I_2 \) and \( h = \alpha^{2} I_3 \), the kernel is trivial when \( \alpha = 1 \), leaving only \( U(1) \) embedded into \( SU(5) \).

**Conclusion**

Therefore, \( \phi: G \rightarrow H \) is a surjective group homomorphism with a trivial kernel, establishing the embedding of the Standard Model gauge group \( G \) into the Georgi-Glashow gauge group \( H = SU(5) \).

The Georgi-Glashow model is a grand unified theory that unifies the Standard Model gauge group into
`SU(5)`.

This file currently contains informal-results about the Georgi-Glashow group.

-/

namespace GeorgiGlashow

/-- The homomorphism of the Standard Model gauge group into the Georgi-Glashow gauge group, i.e.,
the group homomorphism `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) → SU(5)` taking `(h, g, α)` to
`blockdiag (α ^ 3 g, α ^ (-2) h)`.

See page 34 of https://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/guts.pdf
-/
informal_definition inclSM where
  deps := [``GaugeGroupI, ``StandardModel.GaugeGroupI]
